hero.title: Designing clarity in complex systems
hero.subtext: From real-world complexity to decision-ready systems.
hero.positioning:
We don’t design dashboards.
We design how decisions get made.

featuredProject.opening:
We don’t measure particles.
We translate invisible systems.
featuredProject.subtext: From fragmented environmental data to decision-ready systems.
featuredProject.positioning: A system for making irreversible decisions — where confidence comes from structure, not intuition.

columns.problemBody: Environmental programs generate constant signals, but decisions lag behind. Data arrives without meaning, context lives in too many places, and accountability breaks when conditions shift.
columns.systemBody: SiVeCa connects sensors, environmental variables, regulatory frameworks, and user decisions — turning raw readings into an interpretable chain from signal → implication → response.
columns.outcomeBody: A shift from monitoring to intelligence: clearer thresholds, faster alignment, and decisions that hold up under scrutiny — because the structure is explicit.

systemsSection.title: Systems I work on
systemsSection.lead: I work across systems where clarity is critical:

approach.title: How I think — a loop, not a checklist
approach.intro: Most products fail at the structure level, not the interface.

steps.title: Frame
steps.text: Name the user, the risk, and the decision the product optimizes for — in language stakeholders can stress-test.

steps.title: Model
steps.text: Map objects, states, and handoffs. What stays visible; what sits one deliberate layer deeper.

steps.title: Prototype
steps.text: Flows and copy as one surface. Can people explain what happened — not only that they clicked through?

steps.title: Ship
steps.text: Instrument for learning, tighten edge cases, leave patterns that make the next release faster.

about.title: Grounded in how systems actually behave
about.body: I work with teams in regulated, technical, and politically sensitive spaces — where ambiguity has a cost and every session has to earn trust.

pillars.title: Systems
pillars.body: Incentives, constraints, and feedback loops first — so the product scales without losing coherence.

pillars.title: Product
pillars.body: Scope, sequencing, and the narrative teams need when trade-offs are unavoidable.

pillars.title: Environment
pillars.body: Durable patterns, accessible defaults, and honest lifecycle thinking for work that leaves a footprint.

contact.title: Let’s build something that holds under pressure.
contact.body: For collaborations, advisory work, or deep dives on systems-heavy products — send context and timeline.
